title: FDA De Novo review of OsteoDetect: 24 clinicians detect wrist fractures more accurately with AI
summary: In the reader study that FDA reviewed for OsteoDetect, 24 clinicians found distal radius fractures with 80.3% sensitivity when aided, against 74.7% unaided.
account: Imagen Technologies of New York makes OsteoDetect, machine learning software that marks distal radius fractures on wrist X-rays. In a fully crossed reader study, 24 clinicians read 200 cases with and without the software, with at least one month between sessions. The readers were radiologists, orthopedic surgeons, emergency physicians, emergency physician assistants, internists and family physicians. Three hand surgeons set the ground truth. FDA reviewers report that the area under the ROC curve rose from 0.840 unaided to 0.889 aided. Sensitivity rose from 74.7% to 80.3% and specificity from 88.9% to 91.4%. Every type of reader improved. FDA granted the De Novo request on 24 May 2018. The study used archived images, so it measured reader accuracy and did not measure patient outcomes.
purpose: OsteoDetect was built to help clinicians detect distal radius fractures on wrist X-rays. Better detection is that purpose.

ratings.reason: Aided clinicians reached 80.3% sensitivity and 91.4% specificity against 74.7% and 88.9% unaided.

ai_role.statement: Every reader read every case with and without the software in a crossed design, so the gain is attributed to the software.
